parameters.content:
## Order Reconciliation | 02 Source A Parse and Clean
Module 2 of 8. Picks up file_runs rows left status=received by Module 1 with source_type=source_a, downloads and parses each file, normalizes every row against client_config's column map, validates it, deduplicates at the order_ref+line_no level, and resolves field-level conflicts instead of overwriting.

**Reads:** client_config, file_runs, canonical_lines (per client, refreshed every loop iteration).
**Writes:** canonical_lines (upsert), exceptions (upsert), file_runs.status=parsed, run_summary.
**Does not:** currency conversion, discount/VAT, credit check, commission (Module 5/6). Does not touch Source B or C (Module 3).

## Before first run
1. Fill Set Environment Config, including the new canonical_lines table id.
2. Add column_map_json, status_map_json, valid_currencies_json, date_formats to client_config (see setup guide).
3. Run Module 1 first so file_runs has status=received rows for source_a.

## Why the canonical-lines lookup is inside the loop
It is re-queried fresh on every file, not loaded once before the loop. That way day 2's duplicate check sees rows day 1 just wrote in the same run, and a rerun always checks against what Airtable actually holds rather than a stale in-memory snapshot.

## Conflict resolution is per field
When two versions of the same order line disagree, each field is compared on its own: fields that agree keep their value, fields that disagree are set to null and listed in conflict_fields. Every version seen is preserved in conflict_values_json. Nothing is silently picked.

## Handoff
Module 3 reads canonical_lines (intake_status in clean, review, conflict) alongside Source B and C to reconcile across all three sources. Rejected rows are excluded from that stage entirely.
